text:
Ville Koivunen won it for Pittsburgh at 3:44 of overtime, a snap shot off passes from Hendrix Lapierre and Kris Letang, and it capped a night in which PIT spent most of the game on the attack. Koivunen was drafted 51st overall by Carolina in 2021 out of Karpat Jr., and he was named first star.

The score makes this look tight. Our numbers say it wasn't. PIT out-attempted NSH 73 to 45 and led in expected goals (the quality of chances, not just the count) 4.37 to 2.89. By our deserved-to-win measure, the share of simulated replays of every shot that a team wins, PIT came out ahead 78 percent of the time. The biggest gap came in the second period, 1.95 to 0.91, and that was the period in which Jayden Struble put NSH up 2-1. NSH's opener came from Steven Stamkos on a deflection in the first, a 22 percent chance by our model.

Juuse Saros is the reason it stayed close. He stopped 34 of 37 shots and saved 1.4 goals more than the quality of those shots deserved, including a 51 percent look for Elmer Soderblom in the first. Rickard Rakell finally beat him with 66 seconds left in regulation, a snap shot from Sidney Crosby and Erik Karlsson that made it 2-2. That sent it to overtime, where NSH had only 0.35 expected goals against it but no answer once Koivunen found the puck. Arturs Silovs made 24 saves for PIT, and the PIT forwards on the ice with Koivunen were comfortably ahead on chances. The facts we have don't include either team's record or streak, so this is one game, and it was PIT's by the way it was played as well as the way it ended.
